config.title: Arrays & Iterators

intro.title: Arrays & Iterators
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that manages a list of your favorite movies. You will learn how to create and manipulate arrays, which are used to store collections of data in JavaScript. The core concepts include using array methods like push, pop, and forEach to add, remove, and loop through items. By the end, you'll understand how to use iterators to process each element in an array efficiently.
intro.usecase: Arrays and iterators are fundamental to building dynamic user interfaces in modern web applications. You'll use them to render lists of data like product catalogs in e-commerce sites, display user notifications in social media feeds, or populate dropdown menus in forms. When building dashboards that show analytics charts or tables, arrays store the data points while iterators transform and display them. Every time you filter search results, sort a table, or paginate content, you're working with arrays and their iteration methods.

objectives: Initialize arrays with different data types and access elements using bracket notation
Manipulate array contents by adding and removing elements from both ends
Apply iterator methods to transform arrays without modifying the original
Construct conditional logic within iterator methods to filter array elements
Integrate multiple iterator methods to process data through sequential operations
Configure accumulator patterns to reduce arrays into single computed values
Implement array iteration to dynamically render content in the DOM

steps.title: Create an array of numbers
steps.instruction: Create a variable called 'numbers' and assign it an array containing the numbers 1 through 5.
steps.hint: Use the array literal syntax with square brackets [] and separate each number with commas.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an array of strings
const fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'orange'];
steps.expectedOutcome: You have a variable named 'numbers' storing [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
successCriteria: The variable 'numbers' is declared and assigned an array containing the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your array contains exactly the numbers 1 through 5 in order.
steps.feedbackWrong: use square brackets [] to create an array and include the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.

steps.title: Access array elements
steps.instruction: Create a variable called 'firstNumber' that gets the first element of the numbers array, and a variable called 'thirdNumber' that gets the third element.
steps.hint: Array indices start at 0. Use bracket notation with the index to access each element.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];

// Access the first and third elements here
steps.expectedOutcome: firstNumber is 1 and thirdNumber is 3 (from indices 0 and 2 of numbers).
successCriteria: Variables firstNumber and thirdNumber are declared and assigned values from the numbers array using bracket notation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Make sure both variables are assigned using numbers[0] and numbers[2].
steps.feedbackWrong: Create two variables: firstNumber from numbers[0] and thirdNumber from numbers[2].

steps.title: Modify array elements
steps.instruction: Update the second element in the numbers array (index 1) to the value 10.
steps.hint: Use bracket notation to assign a new value: numbers[1] = 10.
successCriteria: The element at index 1 is changed to 10.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Make sure you assign 10 to numbers[1].
steps.feedbackWrong: Use numbers[1] = 10 to update the second element.

steps.title: Modify the last element
steps.instruction: Update the last element in the numbers array to the value 25.
steps.hint: Use numbers[numbers.length - 1] = 25 to change the last element.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 10, 3, 4, 5];

// Update the last element to 25 here
successCriteria: The last element is changed to 25 using bracket notation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've updated the last element correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: Assign 25 to the last element: numbers[numbers.length - 1] = 25.

steps.title: Add to end with push()
steps.instruction: Add the number 6 to the end of the numbers array using the push() method.
steps.hint: Call numbers.push(6). This modifies the array in place.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 10, 3, 4, 25];

// Add 6 to the end using push() here
successCriteria: The push() method is called on numbers with the argument 6.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an element to the end using push().
steps.feedbackWrong: Call numbers.push(6) to add 6 to the end of the array.

steps.title: Add to start with unshift()
steps.instruction: Add the number 0 to the beginning of the numbers array using the unshift() method.
steps.hint: Call numbers.unshift(0). This modifies the array in place.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 10, 3, 4, 25, 6];

// Add 0 to the beginning using unshift() here
successCriteria: The unshift() method is called on numbers with the argument 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackWrong: Call numbers.unshift(0) to add 0 to the beginning.

steps.title: Remove from end and start
steps.instruction: Remove the last element from the numbers array using pop(),
steps.hint: Call numbers.pop() then numbers.shift(). Both modify the array in place.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [0, 1, 10, 3, 4, 25, 6];

// Remove last with pop(), then first with shift() here
steps.expectedOutcome: After pop() and shift(), the numbers array becomes [1, 10, 3, 4, 25].
successCriteria: pop() is called to remove the last element, and shift() is called to remove the first element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: remove the first element using shift()
steps.instruction: remove the first element using shift().
steps.hint: Call numbers.pop() then numbers.shift(). Both modify the array in place.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [0, 1, 10, 3, 4, 25, 6];

// Remove last with pop(), then first with shift() here
steps.feedbackPartial: Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Iterate with forEach()
steps.instruction: Use the forEach() method on the numbers array to log each number to the console with the prefix 'Number: '.
steps.hint: Call numbers.forEach() with a callback that receives each element and logs it with console.log('Number: ', element) or similar.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 10, 3, 4, 25];

// Use forEach() to log each number with prefix 'Number: ' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The console logs: Number: 1, Number: 10, Number: 3, Number: 4, Number: 25 (one per line).
successCriteria: forEach() is called on numbers with a callback that logs each element with the prefix 'Number: '.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use numbers.forEach() and include 'Number: ' in the log.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use numbers.forEach() with a callback that logs each element and the 'Number: ' prefix.

steps.title: Transform with map()
steps.instruction: Create a variable called 'doubledNumbers' that holds a new array where each element of numbers is doubled, using the map() method.
steps.hint: Use numbers.map() with a callback that returns each number multiplied by 2.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 10, 3, 4, 25];

// Create doubledNumbers using map() here
steps.expectedOutcome: doubledNumbers is [2, 20, 6, 8, 50] (each element of numbers doubled).
successCriteria: doubledNumbers is declared and assigned using map() on numbers, with each element doubled.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use numbers.map() and multiply each element by 2.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create doubledNumbers using numbers.map() and double each value.

steps.title: Filter with filter()
steps.instruction: Create a variable called 'evenNumbers' that holds a new array containing only the even numbers from the numbers array, using the filter() method.
steps.hint: Use numbers.filter() with a callback that returns true when the number is even (number % 2 === 0).
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 10, 3, 4, 25];

// Create evenNumbers using filter() here
steps.expectedOutcome: evenNumbers is [10, 4] (the even values from numbers).
successCriteria: evenNumbers is declared and assigned using filter() on numbers with a callback that checks for even numbers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use numbers.filter() with a callback that returns true when n % 2 === 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use numbers.filter() to keep only elements where number % 2 === 0.

steps.title: Sum with reduce()
steps.instruction: Create a variable called 'sum' that holds the total of all numbers in the numbers array, using the reduce() method.
steps.hint: Use numbers.reduce() with a callback (accumulator, current) => accumulator + current and initial value 0.
steps.seedCode:
const numbers = [1, 10, 3, 4, 25];

// Create sum using reduce() here
successCriteria: sum is declared and assigned using reduce() on numbers to add all elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've used reduce() to compute the sum.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use numbers.reduce() with (acc, n) => acc + n and initial value 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use numbers.reduce() to add all elements; start with 0 as the initial accumulator.
